bug: The prior file's openrocket_stage_id block stated 's0 ignites at t=0 (launch)' and 's1 ignites at burnout of s0', which is the OPPOSITE of the physical event sequence and contradicts that same file's own component_ownership_check (branch 1/booster separates/hits ground at t~30.3s after a short t=2.5s drop -- i.e. branch 1 fired FIRST, at launch).
verification_method: Direct inspection of artifacts/autoevo/best-legal-booster-branch.ork's rocket.ork XML (unzipped), not prose.

stage_0.name: Sustainer
stage_0.main_motor_ignition_meaning: Ignites when the PREVIOUS stage's (Booster's) main motors burn out -- i.e. after separation, not at launch.

retro_motor_ignition.meaning: Effectively disabled for this candidate -- 200s past launch is after the flight ends.

stage_1.name: Booster
stage_1.main_motor_ignition_meaning: Ignites AT LAUNCH (t=0) -- the booster provides initial thrust.
stage_1.retro_motor_ignition_meaning: Ignites 29.864s after LAUNCH (t=0), NOT after booster main-motor burnout or separation. This is an ABSOLUTE mission-time delay, confirmed directly in the XML (ignitionevent=launch, not ignitionevent=burnout).

event_log_corroboration.component: Sustainer Main Motor Mount (stage 0) -- fires at booster main-motor burnout/separation
Sustainer Structural Retro Sleeve (stage 0) -- inert, past flight end
Booster Structural Retro Sleeve (stage 1) -- H180W retro/landing motor

corrected_physical_event_sequence: t=0: Booster (stage 1) main motors ignite at launch.
t=~2.5s: Booster main motors burn out; STAGE_SEPARATION fires.
t=~2.5s: Sustainer (stage 0) main motors ignite (ignitionevent=burnout of stage 1).
t=29.864s (absolute, from launch): Booster retro motor (H180W) ignites -- scheduled by ignitionevent=launch + ignitiondelay, NOT relative to booster burnout or separation.
t=~30.79s: Booster ground contact (powered, motor still burning).
t=~31.18s: Booster retro motor burns out (after ground contact -- see burn_remaining_at_contact_s).
component_tree_vs_ignition_are_independe: OpenRocket's stage NUMBER (0=top/Sustainer, 1=bottom/Booster, fixed by component-tree build order) is a different axis from ignition ORDER (Booster/stage-1 fires first at launch, Sustainer/stage-0 fires second at stage-1 burnout). The former is structural; the latter is a per-motor-mount ignitionconfiguration. The prior file conflated 'lower stage number' with 'ignites first', which is wrong for this two-stage-with-lower-booster topology.

retro_delay_convention.s1_retro_delay: ABSOLUTE seconds from LAUNCH (t=0), via ignitionevent=launch + ignitiondelay=s1_retro_delay in the XML. NOT relative to booster burnout, separation, or apogee.
retro_delay_convention.s0_retro_delay: Same convention (ignitionevent=launch, ignitiondelay=s0_retro_delay), independently of s0's own main-motor ignitionevent=burnout.
